# QR Code Handling

A user pastes a QR image with "帮我扫一下 / 你能帮我操作吗". The order is fixed:
**decode → classify → decide → act**. The task is almost always decided at the
classify step, not the decode step.

## 1. Decode (no zbar, no system cv2 needed)

```bash
cd /tmp && uv run --quiet --with opencv-python-headless --with numpy python3 - <<'EOF'
import cv2
img = cv2.imread('<path>.png', cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE)
data, pts, _ = cv2.QRCodeDetector().detectAndDecode(img)
print('DATA:', repr(data))
EOF
```

Empty result on a screenshot is the common case (too few pixels per module).
Retry upscaled and binarized:

```python
big = cv2.resize(img, None, fx=3, fy=3, interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
_, th = cv2.threshold(big, 128, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)
# try detectAndDecode(big) and detectAndDecode(th)
```

Print the **entire** payload including query params — the host alone rarely
says what it is; the path and token params do.

## 2. Classify before touching anything

| Payload | What it is | Correct move |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary URL, promo, `WIFI:T:...`, vCard, plain text | grants no authority | fetch/read read-only if useful, answer |
| Device/login verification token (`accounts.google.com/devicephoneverification/*`, web-login QR for WhatsApp/Telegram/WeChat/Discord, device-pairing QR) | **a one-time credential**: whoever consumes it *becomes* the trusted device / signed-in client | see the rule below |
| `otpauth://` (TOTP secret), password-reset or invite token | secret material | never render or forward it; name it and stop |
| Payment (`weixin://`, `alipay://`, UPI, card setup) | money moves | user completes it; never act |

Give the decoded payload and its class in one line *before* any action — the
user cannot judge the risk of a token they can't read.

## 3. Never consume an auth/verification token on the user's behalf

Scanning a login or device-verification QR makes **your** browser the device
that approves it. That is not "helping their session along": a new or
newly-signed-in account gets anchored to your machine, your IP and your
fingerprint — exactly the pattern providers auto-suspend, so the user ends up
with a dead account while believing verification succeeded. For an existing
account it is silent device-binding on hardware that isn't theirs.

So: decode, explain, and fix the *user's* path. If their phone has no network,
make the phone reach the service (`network-egress-diagnosis`) instead of scanning
for them. Keep "what I verified" and "what is my judgement" in separate
sentences — this is the class of task where guessing reads as fact.

## 4. Ground the answer in what the page actually said

Check the token read-only, without consuming it:

```bash
curl -sSL -m 25 -o /tmp/p.html -w 'final=%{url_effective} code=%{http_code}\n' "<url>"
```

- `200` + redirect to an `.../initiate`-style path ⇒ token is live; you can say
  that as fact.
- JS-only pages (`Loading`, empty `innerText`) do not self-describe their
  requirements. Say "页面只说 Verify your phone，需要哪台设备这一步看不出来" rather
  than inventing a requirement.

# Google `devicephoneverification` QR (account creation / sign-in)

Observed directly on this box:

- Payload: `https://accounts.google.com/devicephoneverification/begin?hl=en&flow=browser&plt=<long token>&dsh=S-<id>:<epochms>`
- `begin` 302s to `.../devicephoneverification/initiate?...` with the same `plt`.
- The static DOM carries only `Verify your phone` + a `Loading` state: no
  account, no number, no instructions.

## Roles

- **Desktop browser**: shows the QR and polls for the result; the `plt` token is
  bound to *that* in-progress session.
- **Phone**: opens the QR URL and acts as the verifying device. Google expects a
  device it recognises as a phone (Google app / Android / carrier SIM). The phone
  ends up bound in the new account's trust chain with its first-login IP.

## Why an agent browser must not complete it

- A Linux Chrome behind a proxy is not the device class being asked for; the page
  most plausibly never offers a usable confirm affordance (judgement — the page
  did not say).
- If it did, the account's verifying device and first IP would become an agent's
  proxy egress. New Google accounts verified from flagged proxy ranges are
  routinely disabled on first sign-in — the user gets a dead account while
  believing verification succeeded.
- Whoever scans it has, functionally, authority to bind the account. Treat the
  token like a password: don't forward it, don't paste it into other services,
  don't leave it in a screenshot.

## What to tell the user instead

1. Name it: "这是谷歌给你这次注册会话发的一次性手机验证令牌，谁扫谁就是代你验证的那台设备".
2. Give the phone egress from a machine that already has it (LAN proxy, hotspot,
   VPN on the phone). Verify the config and the Windows-side listener before
   instructing them, and be explicit that only the phone opening
   `generate_204` proves the peer path — a WSL-side curl to the host's LAN IP
   tests the guest against itself under mirrored networking
   (`network-egress-diagnosis` Step 3).
3. Offer `Try another way` on the signup page (email verification) as the
   no-network fallback.
